clue.text: Nuclear deterrence is possible, according to the president

parts.note: MAD stands for Mutually Assured Destruction, the doctrine of nuclear deterrence
taken as written
on, as in 'that's not on', means feasible or possible

explanation.surface: A politician declares that nuclear deterrence remains a viable option, citing the head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'according to' is a link joining the wordplay to the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: James Madison was the fourth president of the United States.

clue.text: Napoleon of crime with sequel to memento of an aesthete

parts.note: the Latin phrase memento mori, a reminder of death, has this word following memento
arty describes someone with artistic pretensions, like an aesthete

explanation.surface: A criminal mastermind is linked to a follow-up to some keepsake of an art lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Holmes called his arch-enemy Professor Moriarty 'the Napoleon of crime'; the answer runs across 1 and 22 down.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Sherlock Holmes stories, the professor is described by the detective as the Napoleon of crime.

clue.text: Wait on your toes when news is due between reels

indicators.note: the news time is placed between two copies of the dance word, splitting them

parts.note: reels are lively dances, so the plural gives the word dance twice
the BBC's 'News at Ten' arrives at ten o'clock

explanation.surface: A dancer waits nervously on tiptoe between reels for the news bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'reels' supplies two dances, with AT TEN (from 'News at Ten', the British evening bulletin) sitting between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to serve someone obsequiously, waiting on them hand and foot; 'on your toes' fits the dance image.

clue.text: Joint meshing of lips making a lot of noise

indicators.note: meshing suggests the letters of lips being interlaced into a new order

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A loud kiss: a mouth meeting another with a lot of noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meshing of' is the anagram signal on lips; 'Joint' is slang, not a body part or hinge, and 'making' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A spliff is slang for a cannabis cigarette, commonly called a joint.

clue.text: See you don't skate here!

definitions.meaning: to see is to observe or spot something
read as two words, a warning that the surface is not frozen water

explanation.definitionFit: To see something is to observe it, which is the verb's ordinary meaning.

clue.text: 151 mice deaths involved in such questions?

definitions.text: 151 mice deaths involved in such questions?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up together, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: 151 in Roman numerals is CLI
taken as written

explanation.surface: Laboratory animals dying raises a certain kind of moral question.
explanation.walkthrough: CLI, the Roman numeral 151, plus MICE DEATHS make the anagram fodder; the whole clue is also the definition, since animal deaths in experiments raise exactly these issues.
explanation.definitionFit: Moral questions about medical research, such as killing laboratory mice, belong to this field of professional principles.

clue.text: Labels fellow a good shot

parts.note: to mark items is to label them
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: Someone tags a man as an excellent shooter.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman is a person skilled at hitting targets, an expert shooter.

clue.text: Stop one going hell for leather, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken and the sound is what counts

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, hell; suede is a type of leather

explanation.surface: Someone tries to halt a person dashing off at top speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hell for leather' looks like the idiom for great speed, but it means DIS followed by SUEDE, which said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissuade someone from going is to persuade them not to, stopping them.

clue.text: Rice familiarly covering carriages with new cadet wanting what isn't good for him

indicators.note: covering means one word wraps round the other

parts.note: Condoleezza Rice, US Secretary of State, was known familiarly as Condi
a train is a line of carriages

indicators.note: new means the letters of cadet are made afresh in another order

explanation.surface: A politician nicknamed after rice escorts a fresh recruit lacking what is harmful to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CADET to CATED; 'with' and 'wanting' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A contraindicated drug or treatment is one that is inadvisable, harmful for a particular patient.

clue.text: Clue (not the first) about little bag for slippery creature who became Mrs Ferrars

indicators.note: about means the trimmed word sits around the other pieces
not the first says the initial letter of the clue word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
a cyst is a small sac or bag in the body
an eel is famously slippery

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter describes a deceitful woman who married into the Ferrars family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slippery creature' looks like part of the definition but belongs to the wordplay; 'for' is a link. The heroine is the schemer in Jane Austen's Sense and Sensibility.
explanation.definitionFit: In Austen's novel, this character marries Robert Ferrars and so becomes Mrs Ferrars.

clue.text: Learn structure of kidneys

indicators.note: structure suggests the letters of learn are built into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A medical student studies how the kidneys are built.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal is the adjective relating to the kidneys.

clue.text: I'm blowing my own trumpet, thank you — about time for a sort of boom

indicators.note: about means the thanks word is placed around the time abbreviation

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you
hr is short for hour, a unit of time
a sonic boom is the noise of a supersonic aircraft

explanation.surface: A boaster thanks people for the noise of a supersonic jet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the time inside the thanks; 'for' is a link. Ta is everyday British thanks. 'Blowing my own trumpet' sounds like music but is boasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrasonic means boastful, from Thraso, the braggart soldier in a Roman comedy by Terence.

clue.text: Such as 9 and 16 rather than 1 across and 23, they are absolutely not with it

definitions.text: Such as 9 and 16 rather than 1 across and 23
definitions.meaning: nine and sixteen are three and four multiplied by themselves, unlike the New York and Prague places named after other answers

definitions.text: they are absolutely not with it
definitions.meaning: squares are unfashionable people, and perfect ones are completely so

explanation.walkthrough: Madison Square Garden and Wenceslas Square are the squares tied to 1 across and 23.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers that are whole numbers multiplied by themselves, and thoroughly old-fashioned people, both carry this name.

clue.text: Incomplete cover from wicked witch: hang about

indicators.note: about means the hanging word goes round the jumbled letters

parts.note: to scrag is old slang for hanging someone by the neck

indicators.note: wicked suggests the letters of witch behaving badly, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A wicked witch is threatened with hanging and leaves her head half covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' rearranges witch to TCHWI and 'about' wraps the hanging word round it; 'from' is a link. Scrag is old slang for hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratch-wig is a small wig covering only part of the head.

clue.text: See 24
Aim and means of angler that isn't mobile

parts.note: an angler's aim is to land the fish
a fishing line is how the angler catches

explanation.surface: An angler describes his goal and his gear, which is not portable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of angler' serves both pieces: landing the fish is the aim, the line the means. 'Mobile' is the phone, not a moving thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed telephone connection is contrasted with a mobile phone.

clue.text: One needs physician in poor place like Tristan da Cunha

indicators.note: in places the one and the doctor inside the word for poor

parts.note: mean can mean poor or shabby
one is I as a Roman numeral
doc is a familiar name for a doctor

explanation.surface: A remote island community needs a doctor in its impoverished settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristan da Cunha is an island far out in the South Atlantic, a far-flung spot in open sea.

clue.text: Turn up with sailor, with North not South? Yes

definitions.text: Turn up with sailor, with North not South? Yes

indicators.note: turn means the letters are spun round into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the compass letter for north takes the place of the one for south

explanation.surface: Someone rises to join a sailor, swapping the south for the north.
explanation.walkthrough: SAILOR with N replacing S gives NAILOR, which is shuffled with UP; the clue as a whole also describes something having a north pole and no south one.
explanation.definitionFit: Unipolar means having a single pole, such as a magnet with north but not south.

clue.text: Nothing over water in a favourite laxative

indicators.note: in puts the French word inside the favourite

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
rien is French for nothing, the language across the Channel

explanation.surface: A favourite remedy is nothing more than water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over water' signals French, the language spoken across the English Channel from Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperient is a mild laxative medicine.

clue.text: Object of worship not working, they say

indicators.note: they say signals that the words are spoken, so only the sound matters

parts.note: idle means not working

explanation.surface: Something revered is said to be lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an image or person that is worshipped.

clue.text: Rope bringing berries to the Queen

parts.note: haws are the red berries of hawthorn
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A rope used to carry berries to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick rope used for mooring or towing a ship.

clue.text: See 5 across
Accept food — rice, possibly — for 5 across 20, perhaps

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Taking food such as rice is a principle of the doctors' rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the letters of ACCEPT FOOD RICE; 'for' is a link, and 'perhaps' shows the definition is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical ethics is an example of a set of professional rules for conduct.

clue.text: See 1
Virtuous monarch heard asking where girl comes from?

indicators.note: heard signals that the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: whence asks from where, and a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A good king is overheard enquiring about a young woman's origins.
explanation.walkthrough: Good King Wenceslas of the Christmas carol is the virtuous monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol calls the Bohemian duke 'Good King', so a virtuous monarch.

clue.text: Nice try — it may catch the train

definitions.text: Nice try — it may catch the train

indicators.note: may suggests the letters might be put into a different order

explanation.surface: A good attempt: a commuter might just make it to the express.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a passenger may catch this express service, split across 24 and 13.
explanation.definitionFit: InterCity is the British brand name for fast long-distance trains between cities.

clue.text: Two notes: some energy is what all should be (like others' grass?)

definitions.text: what all should be (like others' grass?)

parts.note: G is a note of the scale
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: some means only part of the word energy is taken

explanation.surface: Two musical notes and some energy: everyone should be more environmental, like the grass next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes ENER from energy. The definition plays on environmentalism and the saying 'the grass is always greener on the other side'.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone should be more environmentally friendly, and other people's grass always looks more verdant.

clue.text: Regrettably strayed on the Sabbath

indicators.note: regrettably suggests things went wrong, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone wandered off on Sunday, which is to be regretted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabbath is a weekly day set aside for rest.
